# Saved-state compatibility fixtures

`v0.1.0-hot-state.json` was generated by the unmodified engine and physics modules at commit `fede82c6d6846e4e88636418c321320d5a1cd348` (release v0.1.0):

```js
const plant = new PWRPlant();
plant.setControl('demand', 0.75);
plant.step(60);
const fixture = plant.exportState();
```

It is an actual v1-format state during a transient. It is not a v2 state with its schema label changed. Migration checks use it to detect compatibility regressions. Changed physical closures can alter subsequent results; migration preserves the saved dynamic state rather than promising bit-identical continuation across model versions.

`v0.14.0-paired-recipe.json` was generated with the engine and paired runner from release v0.14.0, commit `5f56c1233bd497be6170295f57d02c6adbeea076`.

```js
const plant = new PWRPlant({ initialPower: 0.73 });
plant.setControl('demand', 0.79);
plant.step(5.15);
const pair = await runPairedExperiment(plant.exportState(), { demand: 0.62, durationS: 12 });
const fixture = pair.recipe;
```

The companion `v0.14.0-paired-output.csv` contains `pairedRunCsv(pair)` from the released code on Node 24.13.0. The compatibility test checks all 13 rows and both branches against that file. Times, commands, trip flags and the recipe itself must match exactly. Numerical readings have a tolerance of 10⁻¹⁰ in their reported units because JavaScript runtimes can round transcendental functions differently. The legacy recipe uses the v2 saturation-curve feedwater model.
